data.text/markdown:
LSTM encoder + LSTM vs MLP decoder: lstm_mlp_dry

Compare two autoregressive CNR predictors sharing the same LSTM encoder:
  • Seq2Seq — LSTM decoder, sliding-window AR rollout with teacher forcing.
  • Seq2Scalar — MLP head on top hidden state, same sliding-window AR rollout.
Encoder compresses CNR + stim features history → hidden state. Decoder (LSTM or MLP) takes hidden state + future stim features → next-step delta CNR. Both use annealed teacher forcing.
param value
source synthetic
hidden_dim 16
num_layers 2
history_len 15
future_len 10
lr 0.001
epochs 50
batch_size 128
patience 20
tf_ratio_start 1.0
tf_ratio_end 0.0
dropout 0.0
mlp_hidden 64
n_mlp_layers 3
dry_run True

Data: 29984 trajectories × 100 timepoints (synthetic) Encoder input: CNR + 9 stim features (u_t, m_t, recency, ewma_fast, ewma_slow, n_5, slope_5, burst_pos, s_cum) over 15 history steps Decoder input: 9 stim features over 10 future steps → predicts CNR Train: 5000 windows | Val: 1250 | Test: 5000

model type params
LSTM decoder (AR + TF) Seq2Seq 7,889
MLP decoder (AR + TF) Seq2Scalar (mlp_hidden=64, n_mlp_layers=3) 14,017
encoder_in=10 | decoder_in=9 | hidden=16 | layers=2 | mps
